metadata.name: Social Liberalism (British New Liberalism)
metadata.description: The social liberal tradition of T. H. Green and L. T. Hobhouse, centred on enabling freedom through public provision and social reform within a market economy.
metadata.scope: The social liberal tradition of T. H. Green and L. T. Hobhouse, centred on enabling freedom through public provision and social reform within a market economy. Revision2 is an incomplete evidence audit of this specified school. Unsupported modern applications and empirical causal comparisons are null/unknown. Neither agreement nor neutrality is inferred from silence. Historical or programme sources are not a complete contemporary incumbent-government record.
metadata.phrase: A society combining civil freedom with education, social security and opportunities that people can actually use.

axes.brief: Hobhouse's New Liberalism combines representative democracy with social conditions for effective participation. Revision2 evidence limit: only the retained numeric items are supported at this question-level resolution; broad principles do not settle the remaining details.
axes.counterEvidence: His second-chamber and referendum proposals qualify simple majoritarianism; financial government remains parliamentary.
